new: Bench mode now shows every story at the same place in front of the headset, however the headset lies: on its side, face up, high or low.
Before measuring, the bench treats the headset as if a person 1.6 m tall stood level, then recentres the story there.
Anchors are lent to a test and come back after it, as settings do.
Each measurement says how the headset really lay and where the story was. A test can still ask for the old way: view as is.
The full test plan now asks for its pictures in two parts, and jumps to the first chapter of Protein crowds, which has only one.
test: On the test place, Quest 3: bench mode on, Enter AR, then lay the headset on its side on the desk. A cloud test with a picture should show the story upright and in front.
Run the same test with the headset face up and then standing: the view numbers and the pictures should match.
With an anchored place saved, run a test: afterwards the story should be back at its anchored place.
Run the full plan: it should finish as two jobs, with no picture refused.
untested: The fixed view on a real headset: how the Quest tracks while it lies still and unworn, and the pictures through passthrough.
With occlusion on, a desk right in front of the lenses can still hide the story.
